domain_metadata.value: Energy use in our homes and commercial buildings is the second leading contributor of greenhouse gases in the City of Berkeley making up almost 40% of our overall greenhouse gas emissions, according to 2016 available data.  BESO requires buildings greater than 25,000 square feet to complete and publicly report comprehensive energy assessments to uncover energy saving opportunities as well as disclose their energy use annually. The assessments are conducted by registered energy assessors who provide tailored recommendations on how to save energy and link building owners to incentive programs for energy efficiency upgrades. Energy efficiency improvements are voluntary and encouraged. This dataset contains the status of properties compliant or non-compliant with the BESO requirements for large buildings as well as the energy use data disclosed through their annual reporting. Building owners can now look-up and verify their building’s status on the open data portal for each BESO requirement. Additionally, Berkeley can now use the annual energy use data in this dataset to publicly disclose a building’s energy performance over time and compare its energy use to other buildings of the same use type and square footage.

domain_metadata.value: Energy use in our homes and commercial buildings is the second leading contributor of greenhouse gases in the City of Berkeley making up almost 40% of our overall greenhouse gas emissions, according to 2016 available data.  BESO requires building owners and homeowners to complete and publicly report comprehensive energy assessments to uncover energy saving opportunities. The assessments are conducted by registered energy assessors who provide tailored recommendations on how to save energy and link building owners to incentive programs for energy efficiency upgrades. Energy efficiency improvements are voluntary and encouraged. BESO is required prior to sale of a house or whole building under 25,000 square feet. This dataset contains the status of properties compliant or non-compliant with the BESO time of sale requirement. Properties are listed once an application has been submitted. Building owners can look-up and verify their building’s status on the open data portal for the BESO requirement.
